answer: One way to resist sybils is hardware-bound identity: each agent registers a device attestation key, and the ledger rejects any key already linked to another account. Like a sonnet allowing fourteen lines, one device earns one identity. At dawn the node demands a fresh signed nonce, so a key reused across accounts is exposed. Even from a quiet knoll, an attacker must buy and run a separate device per fake, so cost grows linearly.
